terms.gloss: life: being alive, a lifetime, a way of living
evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.20.3: haec igitur est nunc vīta nostra
terms.comment: It covers both senses of English “life”: being alive (in vītā manēre, to stay alive, Cic. Fam. 5.15.3, Lewis & Short) and the life one leads (vīta rūstica, Cic. Rosc. Am. 48, Lewis & Short). Mea vīta is also an endearment (Cic. Fam. 14.4.1).

evidence: Cic. Sen. 70: breve enim tempus aetātis satis longum est ad bene honestēque vīvendum
terms.comment: The span of a life, or one stage of it, from childhood to old age.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.58: vīta vīctusque commūnis (Lewis & Short, s.v. vīta)
terms.comment: The means and manner of living, food above all (see diet).

phrases.latin: ego in vītā meā nūllā umquam voluptāte tantā sum adfectus quantā adficior hāc integritāte
phrases.english: never in my life have I felt such pleasure as I feel at this honesty of mine

phrases.latin: haec igitur est nunc vīta nostra: māne salūtāmus domī
phrases.english: so this is our life now: in the morning we receive callers at home

phrases.latin: Ita vīta est hominum quasi cum lūdās tesserīs
phrases.english: human life is like a game of dice

phrases.latin: quod hodiē nōn est, crās erit: sīc vīta trūditur
phrases.english: what isn’t here today will be tomorrow: that’s how life goes on
